title: Head of Marketing Strategy & Operations
description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

ABOUT THIS JOB

We're looking for a Head of Marketing Strategy & Operations to run the business side of marketing. Our marketing team went from two people to 25 this year, organized around four functions: product marketing, brand and consumer, enterprise, and growth. This is the first operations hire on that team. You'll own the marketing budget with Finance, run our planning cycle and operating cadence, keep hiring aligned with the plan, and partner directly with the CMO on how marketing sets priorities and tells its story to the executive team and the board.

It's a role for someone who has sat close to a CMO and a CFO, likes turning ambiguity into a plan people can execute, and is comfortable building the function themselves before building a team.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Budget & Financial Operations

- Own the marketing budget end to end with Finance: allocation across teams and channels, tracking against plan, forecasting, variance flags, and the tradeoff conversations that follow

- Build the layer of visibility leadership needs (spend by team, channel, and program) on top of the spend-tracking tools we already have, so decisions get made with numbers

- Run quarterly, half-year, and annual budget planning, and make marketing's case to Finance and the executive team

- Own marketing's vendor and agency contracts end to end: evaluations, procurement, renewals, and a clear view of what we pay for and why

Planning & Operating Cadence

- Own marketing's planning cycle: translate company goals into marketing objectives, OKRs, and resourced plans, and keep them current as priorities shift

- Bring a point of view. Pressure-test plans, frame the tradeoffs, and help the CMO decide where marketing places its bets

- Design the lightweight processes and internal tools (planning, intake, reporting) that let a 25-person team operate like a much bigger one

- Run the operating rhythm for the marketing leadership team: meetings, all-hands, team-wide readouts, agendas, decisions, and follow-through

- Keep the marketing functions connected so plans, launches, and budgets move together

Executive Partnership

- Partner directly with the CMO on board materials, executive readouts, and strategy documents. Own first drafts and make them data-backed and on-message

- Extend the CMO's reach across the team: surface risks early, chase decisions to closure, and keep priorities clear week to week

- Represent marketing in cross-functional planning with Finance, Sales, and Product

Hiring & Org Operations

- Partner with Talent Acquisition and marketing leads on headcount planning, requisition tracking, and interview process, and keep hiring plans aligned with budget and org design

- Standardize the basics across sub-teams (job descriptions, interview loops, scorecards) and help new leaders land well

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

- 10+ years in marketing strategy and operations, business operations, strategic finance, management consulting, or a similar role supporting a CMO, GM, or business unit leader

- You've owned a sizable marketing or departmental budget end to end and can talk about spend, forecast, and variance the way Finance does

- You've built or run a planning cycle (annual or half-year, OKRs) and an operating cadence for a leadership team

- You've drafted board or executive materials for a senior leader and know the difference between a readout and a narrative

- Experience with headcount planning and hiring operations alongside a Talent team

- You've run vendor evaluations and procurement alongside Finance and kept a clean view of contracts and renewals

- Comfortable as an individual contributor. This is the first ops hire; you'll do the work before you have a team

title: Mapping and Analysis of Family Language in African Union Agreed Language and Hum
description:
1. Background
Fòs Feminista . Fòs Feminista is an International Alliance of more than 200 partners across 40 countries working on the sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice (SRHRJ) of women, girls, and gender-diverse people. In 2026, Fòs Feminista completed a three-decade mapping of how "family" has been used in United Nations agreed language - reviewing 1,441 excerpts across 180 UN documents from 1994 to 2025. That mapping found that a substantial, underused body of UN agreed language already centers individual rights, gender equality, and diverse family forms, offering feminist advocates a propositional foundation to build on rather than only a defensive posture against anti-rights mobilization around "family."
This mapping has not yet been extended to the regional level. The African Union (AU) has its own distinct body of human rights instruments, agreed language, and political dynamics relevant to family, gender equality, and SRHR - including the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (the Maputo Protocol), one of the most progressive regional instruments globally on women’s rights, alongside AU mechanisms with an active record on ending child marriage and other harmful practices. At the same time, the AU is not insulated from anti-rights and anti-gender actors seeking to co-opt family language in multilateral outcomes.
As such, Fòs Feminista is seeking a consultant to conduct a systematic mapping and analysis of family-related language across African Union agreed language and human rights mechanisms to produce a rigorous, regionally grounded evidence base for use in African Union-level advocacy.
2. Purpose and Objectives
The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a systematic, evidence-based mapping of how "family" is defined, referenced, and used across African Union agreed language, in order to:

• Identify where existing AU agreed language already reflects rights-based, gender-equal, and diverse understandings of family, distinguishing this from areas where family language is used restrictively or left unaddressed.

• Produce a citable evidence base to inform feminist advocacy in African Union-level negotiations.

• Identify patterns specific to the African regional context - including but not limited to child marriage, female genital mutilation and other harmful practices, inheritance and marital property rights, and care - grounded in the region’s own instruments and mechanisms.

• Analyze whether language has changed over time, assessing whether it reflects advancement, regression, or stagnation in relation to gender equality and SRHR, and identifying the instruments, sessions or political context associated with such shifts.

• Generate concrete recommendations and draft rights-based language proposals for use in AU Summit declarations, Specialized Technical Committee outcomes, and other AU negotiating processes.

3. Scope of Work
The consultant will review family-related language across the following African Union instruments and mechanisms, at minimum:

• The African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights (1981) and its jurisprudence.

• The Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (Maputo Protocol, 2003), with particular attention to its marriage, family, and inheritance provisions.

• The African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (1990).

• Decisions, declarations, and resolutions of the AU Assembly of Heads of State and Government and the Executive Council.

• Resolutions, General Comments, and Concluding Observations of the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights (ACHPR).

• General Comments and Concluding Observations of the African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (ACERWC).

• The Solemn Declaration on Gender Equality in Africa (2004) and subsequent AU gender policy instruments.

• The Plan of Action on the Family in Africa (2004), adopted

title: Equipment Engineer - Automation
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Missions and activities of the position

1. Project phase - owner's engineer for Maintenance

• Represent Maintenance in every phase of new equipment projects (starting with the MRS1 cross-belt sorter), from design reviews to FAT, SAT, commissioning and ramp-up. For the sorter, whose design is already set, take over the installed system and optimise it after go-live.

• Work side by side with the OEM / integrator engineers: collect technical knowledge, challenge design choices, maintainability, access, spare-part strategy and the proposed maintenance plan before they are frozen.

• Define and verify the Maintenance acceptance criteria (documentation, training, spare parts, safety, availability targets). The Maintenance sign-off is mandatory: no handover to operations without it.

• Track and drive to closure the technical punch list and warranty issues raised during commissioning and the warranty period.

2. Technical file & spare parts

• Build and own the equipment technical file: as-built electrical and mechanical drawings, PLC and software versions, parameter backups, network architecture, safety documentation, OEM manuals.

• Create the asset hierarchy and criticality analysis in the CMMS.

• Define the critical spare-parts list (references, min/max stock, lead times) and keep it up to date.

• Reduce dependency on the OEM: identify and qualify second-source suppliers for critical parts, run compatibility tests and document equivalences.

• Propose spare-parts and supplier decisions to the Maintenance Manager; after an initial period, take these decisions autonomously within agreed limits, with the Maintenance Manager's validation.

3. Maintenance strategy & procedures

• Write and maintain preventive maintenance plans, corrective procedures and troubleshooting guides for the equipment family, based on OEM data, FMEA and field experience.

• Monitor equipment performance (availability, MTBF, MTTR, top failure modes), lead root-cause analysis on recurring or major failures and implement permanent corrective actions.

• Challenge the original design when needed and drive engineering changes: retrofits, drive and firmware updates, software or parameter optimisation, with the OEM and internal stakeholders.

4. Training & technical support

• Train the operational maintenance team (technicians and operatives) on the equipment, its software/HMI and the troubleshooting procedures; validate their autonomy level.

• Act as the level-2 / level-3 technical expert for the equipment family on site and remotely

Merlin (NASDAQ: MRLN) is a publicly traded aerospace and defense company building a non-human pilot to deliver full-stack autonomy for any aircraft from takeoff to touchdown. The Merlin Pilot autonomy system powers a growing range of aircraft and mission profiles and has been proven through hundreds of autonomous flights from Merlin's global flight test facilities, including Kerikeri, New Zealand; Smithfield, Rhode Island; and soon, Bedford, Massachusetts. Headquartered in Boston, Merlin is expanding its organization to accelerate the development and deployment of its autonomy platform, helping customers solve some of aviation's most pressing challenges, from pilot shortages to improving flight safety. You are a systems engineering Technology leader who has built and run the function strategically, not just practiced it. ABOUT US

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like - and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia - many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact - this is the place.

ABOUT THE ROLE AND YOU

We're hiring a Demand Generation Lead to own pipeline generation for North America. Today, demand gen at Lorikeet is spread across several people who each carry a piece of it alongside their day jobs - this role exists to change that. You'll be the first person whose sole focus is building the machine that fills our pipeline.

You'll own a North American pipeline target and work backwards from it - designing and executing the mix of events, webinars, industry programs, and campaigns that gets us there. You'll also help shape how demand gen scales as a function as we grow, defining the playbook rather than inheriting one. This is a mid-senior role for someone who's comfortable being accountable to a hard revenue-linked number with a high degree of autonomy over how they hit it.

- Build the demand gen operating infrastructure from scratch: campaign tracking, attribution, and reporting that give us a real view of the funnel

- Identify which channels and plays are worth scaling and which to kill, iterating quickly with limited resources

- Define the demand gen playbook for Lorikeet as we grow, laying the foundation for the function's future team and budget

THE RIGHT CANDIDATE

We're looking for someone who is energized by owning a number, not just running programs - someone who sees a pipeline target as a puzzle to reverse-engineer rather than a burden. The ideal candidate learned the fundamentals of demand gen inside a rigorous, well-resourced marketing org, then proved they could build the whole thing from scratch with none of that scaffolding.

You might be a fit if you:

- Have 4-7 years of demand generation experience in B2B SaaS

- Spent your foundational years at a public software company where you learned what best-in-class demand gen looks like

- Then spent 2-3 years at an early-stage startup (under ~100 people) building the demand gen function from zero - choosing channels, setting up systems, and owning outcomes without a big team or budget

- Have hands-on experience across the program mix: field events, webinars, executive dinners, and industry programs, not just digital campaigns

title: Principal, Talent & Leadership Development
description:
Who are we?

Smarsh empowers its customers to manage risk and unleash intelligence in their digital communications. Our growing community of over 6500 organizations in regulated industries counts on Smarsh every day to help them spot compliance, legal or reputational risks in 80+ communication channels before those risks become regulatory fines or headlines.  Relentless innovation has fueled our journey to consistent leadership recognition from analysts like Gartner and Forrester, and our sustained, aggressive growth has landed Smarsh in the annual Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing American companies since 2008.

We are looking for an experienced, hands-on talent leader to build a culture that raises the bar on talent: where leaders know what great looks like, how to spot it, and how to grow it.
This person will build talent and leadership programs largely from the ground up using industry-leading practices, lead how we attract, identify, develop and promote high-potential talent, and evaluate, select, and bring in AI-driven talent practices, including predictive talent forecasting, for better and faster talent decisions. This role is about knowing the AI talent-tech landscape deeply and choosing and deploying the right platforms, whether vendor or in-house, not building AI models or algorithms from scratch.
This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports. Impact comes through influence rather than authority: partnering with HR business partners and business leaders, earning credibility with senior executives, and using evidence and expertise to drive adoption of talent practices across the organization.
This work is as much about organizational design and change management as it is about building programs: getting the structure, roles, and processes right, and then leading the change management needed for leaders across the organization to adopt and sustain new ways of working.
We are a U.S.-based company operating globally, with colleagues across 10 countries. Programs need to work well beyond the U.S., which means designing with cultural differences in mind from the start and planning for translation and localization of content, not treating them as an afterthought.

Don't meet every requirement? Apply anyway! We value diverse candidates and encourage applications, even if you don't perfectly match the job description. Studies have shown that some strong candidates may self-select out of the interview process prematurely, at Smarsh we encourage an inclusive, high-performing environment.

About our culture

Smarsh hires lifelong learners with a passion for innovating with purpose, humility and humor. Collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. We work closely with the most popular communications platforms and the world’s leading cloud infrastructure platforms. We use the latest in AI/ML technology to help our customers break new ground at scale. We are a global organization that values diversity, and we believe that providing opportunities for everyone to be their authentic self is key to our success. Smarsh leadership, culture, and commitment to developing our people have all garnered Comparably.com Best Places to Work Awards. Come join us and find out what the best work of your career looks like.

title: Product Design Manager
description:
What We Do

We’re on a mission to empower animal healthcare professionals with opportunities to earn more and achieve greater flexibility in their careers and personal lives.

Powered by groundbreaking technology, Roo has built the industry-leading veterinary staffing platform, connecting Veterinarians, Technicians, and Assistants with animal hospitals for relief work and hiring opportunities. Roo empowers the largest network of over 20,000 veterinary professionals to help more than 9,000 animal hospitals provide quality care to more pets.
Together, we’ve provided more than  3 million hours of healthcare, helping Veterinarians earn more than $200 million.

About the Role

We are hiring a design lead: a player-coach for someone who still loves to design while also having a passion to make other designers better.

This role sit within Roo’s product team, which owns product and design craft across the company. The product team supports a number of squads (aka business units), the cross-functional teams accountable for driving the success of the key pillars of our marketplace. Designers are aligned to one or more squads to deliver meaningful business impact but formally sit within the product team to ensure we are creating a cohesive product experience across squads. Holding that tension well is at the core of this job.

As a player-coach, you'll spend real time in Figma owning a few projects end-to-end to drive measurable business impact for one or more business units. At the same time, you’ll help set the quality bar across our full product surface by defining what design excellence means at Roo, and making it stick. You'll grow and coach the team, raise the craft, and build the practices that let design scale with the company.

This role is remote, with occasional travel to our San Francisco co-working space for key meetings and team events.

Responsibilities

• Lead, mentor, and grow the 5 person Product Design team. Support designers in developing strong craft, critical thinking, and strategic influence.

• Evolve our design competencies into a standard the whole company can understand and then make it operate. Today that bar largely lives in people's heads. Making it explicit, defensible, and consistently applied.

• Support career growth by running development conversations, writing performance reviews with business-unit leaders, and making the path from one level to the next clear

• Take on real design work yourself. Everything from hard problems, quick wins, exploratory concepts, and the things that unblock the team.

• Partner with leadership to align design direction with product strategy and company goals.

• Build and strengthen design systems that enable consistency, quality, and scalability. This includes raising the team's leverage with AI by helping to drive forward efforts to make our design system agentic-friendly so prototypes can be built from real components.

• Shape design practices across discovery, concept development, interaction design, prototyping, and delivery.

• Encourage exploration and push the team to rethink assumptions while staying grounded in user needs and market realities.

• Advocate for the customer experience across every surface and ensure design decisions always reflect real customer needs.

Qualifications

• 8+ years of product design experience with 2+ years of management experience

• Demonstrated ability to grow, coach, and support senior designers in improving their craft and helping them extend their skillset from strong execution toward strategic influence

• Strong portfolio demonstrating excellence across visual design, interaction design, systems thinking, product storytelling, and user centered craft.

• Experience building and scaling design systems.

• AI fluency in design practice. You've used AI to move faster on real work and you have a considered view on where it helps and where it produces work that shouldn't ship.

• Ability to bring clarity to ambiguous spaces

title: Customer Support Engineer
description:
We’re always interested in connecting with experienced Customer Support Engineers who could be a great fit for our team as Verge.io continues to grow.

As a Customer Support Engineer at Verge.io , you’ll work directly with customers to help them deploy, operate, and get the most out of VergeOS, troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues and guiding implementations and migrations along the way. It's a hands-on technical role for someone who enjoys solving hard problems and working directly with people.

You’ll also help turn what you learn into better documentation and repeatable processes, using AI as a practical tool to research issues, analyze logs, and find better ways to solve recurring problems.

The Role

You’ll work directly with customers throughout their experience with VergeOS, from implementation and migration through ongoing support, optimization, and upgrades. That includes:

• Troubleshooting and resolving technical issues across the VergeOS platform

• Managing escalations and complex customer inquiries

• Guiding customers through implementations and migrations

• Helping customers optimize their environments and follow platform best practices

• Providing technical guidance for upgrades, maintenance, and other platform changes

• Partnering with Engineering to investigate and resolve complex technical issues

• Documenting technical solutions and contributing to our internal and customer-facing knowledge base

• Identifying recurring issues and turning solutions into repeatable processes

• Using AI to research issues, analyze information, improve responses, and build more efficient support and deployment workflows

• Participating in an on-call rotation as needed

Who You Are

Successful Customer Support Engineers at Verge.io are technical problem-solvers who genuinely enjoy figuring out how things work, and why they sometimes don't.

You’re comfortable digging into Linux, virtualization, networking, logs, and infrastructure configurations to get to the root of a problem. You can work independently when needed, but you also know when to pull in Engineering or other members of the team.

You’re equally comfortable working with people. You can take a complicated technical issue and explain it clearly to a customer, keep communication moving while an issue is being resolved, and build confidence even when the answer isn't immediately obvious.

You also look beyond the individual ticket. When you solve something, you think about how we can document it, automate it, or improve the process so the next customer, and the rest of the team, benefits from what you learned.

The Experience We’re Looking For

We typically look for:

• Significant experience in technical support, infrastructure engineering, systems administration, or a similarly hands-on technical role

• Strong Linux administration skills, ideally within Debian-based environments

• Hands-on experience with virtualization technologies, including KVM/QEMU or similar platforms

• A strong understanding of networking concepts and experience troubleshooting a variety of network configurations

• Experience troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues and working through problems methodically

• Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts clearly

• Experience working directly with customers in a technical capacity

• Comfort working independently in a remote, fast-moving environment

• Practical experience using AI in your work, with examples of how it has helped you research, troubleshoot, automate, document, or work more effectively

Additional Experience That’s Valuable

• Experience in any of the following areas can be especially helpful:

• VMware, Nutanix, Hyper-V, or other virtualization platforms

• AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or other cloud environments

• Scripting or automation using Python, Bash, Go, or similar languages

• REST APIs and systems integrations

• GitHub projects or code samples, particularly projects

title: Harness Engineer, Director
description:
FICO (NYSE: FICO ) is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential!
The Opportunity
As a Director, AI Harness Engineering, you will lead a new internal team that lets AI coding agents do reliable work at scale. As agents take on more of the software lifecycle, the hard part is no longer writing code - agents generate it faster than humans can review it, so the bottleneck shifts to verification and trust. Harness Engineering exists to break that bottleneck: engineering the environment that steers agents toward correct, maintainable, well-architected output so that quality is enforced by the system, not re-audited by a person on every change. We call that environment the harness (Agent = Model + Harness), and we're building a dedicated Harness Engineering team to own it. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will design and build harness components while leading and growing a regional team of harness engineers and setting the quality bar for AI-assisted engineering across the organization.

What You’ll Contribute

• Help design, build, and evolve the harness, the guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that turn raw model capability into production-grade engineering. This is a hands-on role; you will contribute to the development, not just direct it.

• Build and maintain feedforward guides (agent instruction files, reusable skills, architectural rules, reference docs, and codemods) that help agents get it right the first time and drive their adoption across teams.

• Build feedback sensors, custom linters, structural and architecture-fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers - that catch issues automatically before they reach human reviewers.

• Own AI governance for your region: define authority boundaries for what agents may merge unaided, establish LLM testing infrastructure, and ensure AI-generated output meets quality, safety, and compliance thresholds before release.

• Define and own cross-organizational QA and quality-gating standards, ensuring consistent, enforceable engineering practices across teams and product areas.

• Run the steering loop at scale when agents repeat a class of mistake, ensure a control is engineered so it cannot happen again - and treat repository knowledge (docs, specs, context) as the system of record, fighting drift continuously.

• Decide where each control runs in the path to production, fast checks pre-commit, moreexpensive checks post-integration, and continuous sensors that scan for drift outside the changelifecycle - keeping quality as far left as is economical.

title: Technical Product Manager
description:
Facilities Management eXpress is currently seeking a Technical Product Manager to join our team!
Do you build things instead of writing documents about them? Do repeated manual tasks make you want to open your laptop and fix them? If AI coding tools are just how you work, keep reading.
Much of FMX ’s data starts in mechanical rooms, on rooftops, and in partner spreadsheets, and collecting it is slow and expensive. You’ll start by making our Facility Condition Assessments dramatically cheaper and faster. Then you’ll bring that approach to everywhere else data enters FMX .
You’ll be the product manager for these tools and usually the one building them, going from “huh, that’s painful” to a shipped fix in days. You’ll also spend more time on site than anyone in Product, so you’ll be our scout for the problems that never become support tickets.
As the Technical Product Manager, you will:
First priority: make the FCA operation as efficient as possible

• Own the cost and cycle time of an assessment. Baseline cost per building and square foot, technician hours, days on site, report turnaround, and rework rates, then set targets with Professional Services and report on them.

• Tackle the biggest time sinks first, across scoping, on-site capture, data cleanup, report production, and capital plan population.

• Build, ship, and support the FCA tools: the capture app and field workflow, operations tracking, the mapping and floor plan pipeline, and partner data intake.

• Get on site and do the work yourself, interviewing technicians and facilities staff and routing what you learn to the right product manager.

Broader scope: data ingestion and the cost of operations

• Cut the cost of bringing customer data into FMX during onboarding, from equipment lists and floor plans to formats nobody planned for.

• Build tooling that makes data intake repeatable instead of bespoke.

• Improve data completeness, not just speed. Thin data gathered quickly is worse than good data gathered efficiently.

• Use AI where it removes real work, like reading nameplate photos and floor plans, drafting condition narratives, and catching gaps before customers do.

• Automate internal work anywhere a small tool saves real time or money.

• When an internal tool earns a place in the FMX product, make the case and hand it off well, with documentation and data model implications.

• Keep the data defensible. Speed only counts if the work holds up.

What success looks like in year one:

• You know our cost and cycle time per assessment by heart, because you built the reporting.

• Technician hours or days per assessment are measurably down, thanks to what you shipped.

• The field team wouldn’t give up your tools, and Product makes decisions based on what you bring back.

• You’ve applied the same approach to at least one other ingestion problem, likely onboarding, and cut real cost.

A portfolio of shipped work. This matters most. You’ve built and shipped real tools, and you can walk us through what you made, what broke, and how you fixed it.

Daily AI-assisted building. You use tools like Claude, Claude Code, or Cursor every day and have shipped working software with them.

title: Technical Owner
description:
Description
TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We’ve been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners - people with no prior tech background - through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.
As a Technical Owner you’ll own every technical decision behind our programs, from the first conversation with a course author to the bug that never reaches a learner. This is a technical partner role, not a coding job: you weigh each decision against cost, time to learner, and bugs shipped, and you lead one engineer who writes autotests. The role is fully remote and full-time, for candidates based outside the US.
What you will do

•
Own each program’s technical setup. Know its environments, services, providers, and autotests, and keep a written map of what each program depends on.

•
Shape new and updated programs. Collect requirements from authors and constraints from product, test the options, and land on a workable trade-off.

•
Replace what no longer fits. Find, cost, and run the switch when a tool, provider, or setup is outdated or too expensive.

•
Manage providers. Compare offers, negotiate terms, and own integrations with external providers.

•
Lead autotest coverage. Set coverage and priorities for the autotest engineer, and write or fix tests yourself when needed.

•
Be our customer to engineering. Write specs with acceptance criteria for automation, API, and platform needs, and chase each one to done.

•
Cut bugs reaching learners. Trace each bug to where it entered, close the gap with a test, check, or process change, and track the trend.

Requirements
Must have

•
End-to-end technical ownership. 3+ years in engineering, QA automation, or technical operations, including choosing a product’s setup and living with the trade-off after launch.

•
Solid mid-level coding. Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, Git, CI, containers, and REST APIs: enough to read unfamiliar code, fix bugs, and write autotests.

•
English for requirements work. Strong enough to run requirements sessions and write specs engineering teams accept without a round of questions.

Nice to have

•
Leading engineers. Leading or mentoring at least one engineer, ideally in test automation.

•
EdTech and content validation. LMS or autograded courses, QA or release work, or agents that check content for accuracy and freshness.

•
Automation and data stack. Claude Code, MCP, n8n or Make; SQL and dashboards.

What we can offer you

•
Ownership. Real decision-making power in your area: we trust your expertise and don’t micromanage.

•
Remote and flexible. Fully remote collaboration

•
Digital office. Slack, Notion, Miro, and Zoom, with every license you need.

title: Executive Creative Director
description:
About Oxford Road

Oxford Road is the world’s largest podcast advertising agency. We unite brands and creators through strategy and technology for outcomes only we can deliver.

Since the beginning of podcasting, we’ve been here building the playbook, setting the standards, and scaling brands through the power of audio and creator-driven media. Today, we manage campaigns across podcasts, radio, streaming audio, YouTube, and emerging creator platforms for clients that include half of the top advertisers in podcasting.

What really sets us apart? We’re not just buying media. We’re shaping the market itself.

Our thought leadership defines the conversation. Our newsletter reaches thousands of industry decision-makers every week. Our podcast, The Media Roundtable, convenes the most influential voices in audio advertising. Our annual Chief Audio Officer Summit is the premier gathering for marketers, platforms, and creators shaping the future of the medium. Our research (from attribution methodologies to brand safety frameworks) becomes industry standard.

We don’t wait for the market to tell us what’s next. We build it.

The Role

The Executive Creative Director is Oxford Road 's most senior creative leader, accountable for the quality, performance, and culture of everything the Creative department produces across host-read, pre-produced audio, and bespoke 360-degree campaigns. This role owns the creative standard across every client account, not just the highest-profile ones, and is responsible for ensuring that standard is consistently met, measurably tied to results, and strengthened by every test the team runs.

This is a leadership role built around three commitments: quality on everything that ships, creative tied to performance, and testing built in as a standard practice rather than an afterthought. The ECD is the keeper of the craft and the driver of the creative department's contribution to client outcomes, agency growth, and new business.

Scope of Ownership

• Owns creative quality end-to-end across all client accounts: reviewing work in flight before it ships, closing the feedback loop to writers directly, and maintaining a consistent standard across host-read and pre-produced disciplines

• Owns how Audiolytics is used across the department: as a benchmark and coaching tool integrated with compliance and performance data, not as a checkbox exercise

• Owns the talent onboarding, briefing, and feedback process: ensuring every host receives a clear creative jumping-off point, product familiarity, and structured ongoing feedback that improves their reads over time

• Owns the connection between creative output and market performance: working with Analytics and account teams to establish performance baselines and translate results into creative direction

• Owns a test-and-learn culture in partnership with Analytics: bringing creative hypotheses, making testing a standard part of how briefs are written, and ensuring what the team learns shapes the next round of work

• Owns the full creative team: leading and developing writers across Bespoke and Format tiers and producers across host-read and pre-produced disciplines

• Owns key client and talent relationships at the senior creative level: these relationships stay direct, not delegated

• Owns the department's presence in new business pitches: concept development, pitch decks, and demo work, including a repeatable three-ways-in approach (functional, emotional, and host-story angles)

• Owns creative support for bespoke, creator-first partnerships and 360-degree campaigns

• Does not own test design, statistical analysis, or tracking infrastructure; those sit within Analytics

• Does not own production cost, change-order pricing, or P those sit within Finance

Decision Rights

• Final decision-maker on creative quality: what ships and what does not, across all accounts and both production disciplines

• Owns how Audiolytics is applied, evolved, and integrated with complia

title: Senior Security Engineer
description:
Every breach, every failed audit, every new hire stuck in onboarding purgatory traces back to the same question: who has access to what - and should they?

Identity is where modern companies break. Too much access leaks data. Too little grinds the business to a halt. Lumos is the industry's first Autonomous Identity Platform - software that doesn't just surface access risk, but acts on it. We started with a self-service AppStore and grew into the critical infrastructure connecting apps, identities, and data for GitHub, MongoDB, Mars, Pinterest, Anduril, Intercom, Roku, and Netskope. At the center is Albus, our AI agent for identity - mining roles, approving access, and catching the drift humans miss.

You'll ship work that thousands of IT and security teams touch every day. You'll own problems without playbooks, because the category is being redefined in real time - by us.

Why Lumos?

- 🚀 Jump on a rocketship. Since launching out of stealth in April 2022, we've grown from 20 to ~130 Alchemists and raised over $65M from a16z, Scale, Neo, Greg Brockman (President at OpenAI), and Phil Venables (CISO at Google).

- ⭐ Customers love us - and so does the industry. Named a Strong Performer in the 2026 Gartner Voice of the Customer for IGA - 4.7/5, with 96% of reviewers saying they'd recommend us. Our customers cut time-to-access by 98%, slash IT tickets by 72%, and eliminate excess privilege at scale.

- 🏆 A culture worth joining. Three years running on Forbes' Top 100 Best Startup Employers in America (2024, 2025, 2026) - measured on culture, retention, growth, and job creation. That's our Alchemists, not our marketing. See what we live by here https://blog.lumos.com/p/the-anatomy-of-an-alchemist.

As a Senior Security Engineer at Lumos, you’ll shape the identity platform thousands of IT and security teams rely on to protect their data. You’ll build the security foundations every Lumos product runs on and be a trusted voice when our largest customers ask how we keep them safe.

✨ Your Responsibilities

- Design and ship core security platform systems in the Lumos codebase, such as request context propagation across services, scoped API tokens, our authorization service, and decoupling authentication from synced identities.

- Lead multi-sprint security projects end to end, coordinating with engineers on other teams to get them delivered.

- Run security architecture reviews and threat models for new products (for example our MCP Governance gateway and on-device policy checks) before they scale, and turn findings into tracked, prioritized work.

- Drive least-privilege access to our own production systems (databases, data pipelines, AWS IAM, secrets).

- Triage, route, and fix vulnerabilities from pentests, cloud assessments, and dependency scanning, and coordinate retests.

- Take part in security oncall and incident response, and help answer security questions from customers and prospects.

🙌 What We're Looking For

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 3 focused on security (application, product, or platform security).

- A track record of designing, shipping, and operating production security systems, not only reviewing them. Examples: authentication and authorization frameworks, token and session management, secrets management, audit logging.

- Strong backend skills. Python and TypeScript are a strong plus. Go is welcome.

- Clear written communication. You can explain a risk and a trade-off to engineers, PMs, and customers alike.

- Nice to have: identity protocols (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, SCIM), policy engines (OPA, Zanzibar-style models, Cedar), SOC 2 or ISO 27001 environments, general background in IAM, and/or growth-stage startup experience.

- Hands-on experience with threat modeling, secure design review, and finding and fixing vulnerabilities in a real codebase.

- Experience securing cloud infrastructure on AWS (equivalent GCP or Azure experience considered), including IAM and Infrastructure a

title: Data collector / Driver in Lake Charles, LA
description:
Company description
 
Service Measure (SM) is a field data collection company founded in 2013 in New York. 
 
We collect data where automation is not possible. We count features, take pictures, make videos, record speech, and scan areas for every detail you need to make more informed decisions. Our field data collection teams are spread across Europe and North America, ready to accept new challenges.
 
Project objective
 
The goal of the project is to help collect images of streets, main points of interest and public areas in the USA. The project is performed on cars with 360 cameras mounted on top that image the area around the vehicle and store those images on computers inside the vehicle. Later, this data will be used to enhance one the most popular online maps in the world.
 
The data collectors will be given specific routes around public streets and areas, specifically targeting commercial districts and historical sites. Due to poor weather conditions some areas will be visited multiple times in order to collect the best quality of imaging. The project is expected to last from 3 to 6 months and will cover different data collection areas. 
 
The ideal candidate enjoys driving, knows well the area, traffic trends, is highly responsible and reliable.
 
The schedule expected on the project is Monday-Friday, 8 hours/day 40 hours per week. Due to weather downtime, work on weekends is possible.

 
We would be happy to get to know you and your skills better and see how we can support each other's growth.
 
Please apply and let's meet!

We are seeking a security-minded and growth-oriented Senior DataOps Engineer with 6+ years of experience to lead the automation, optimization, and securing of our AWS data ecosystem.
This role is tailor-made for a curious engineer who runs toward complex challenges rather than away from them. You will design next-generation, secure cloud data infrastructure while continuously exploring and learning new AWS services and DevSecOps methodologies to keep our data stack ahead of the curve.

Job title: Senior DataOps Engineer (AWS & Security Focused)
Department: Engineering / Data Engineering
Workplace type: Remote
Experience: 6-12 years
Employment type: Full-time
Requirements
Key Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities

•
AWS Data Infrastructure: Design, deploy, and maintain highly available and scalable data platforms utilizing AWS-native services.

•
Data Security & DevSecOps: Embed security guardrails directly into the data lifecycle. Manage encryption, data masking, network security, and secure access controls.

•
Pipeline Automation (CI/CD): Build and manage automated pipelines for data infrastructure and code deployments using infrastructure-as-code.

•
Orchestration & Governance: Oversee data workflow orchestration and implement real-time security monitoring, logging, and automated compliance auditing.

•
R&D and Continuous Learning: Proactively research, prototype, and implement emerging AWS services and open-source data tools to solve complex infrastructure bottlenecks.

Required Skills & Qualifications

•
Experience: 6+ years of professional experience in DataOps, DevOps, or Data Engineering roles, with a minimum of 4 years dedicated to the AWS ecosystem.

•
Core AWS Stack: Deep hands-on expertise with AWS data and infrastructure services:

•
Compute/Infra: EC2, EKS, ECS, Lambda, Terraform.

•
Data/Analytics: EMR, Glue, Athena, Redshift, S3, Kinesis.

•
AWS Cloud Security: Proficient in securing cloud environments using AWS IAM (least privilege), KMS (encryption at rest/in transit), VPC networking (PrivateLink, Security Groups), Secrets Manager, and AWS GuardDuty/CloudTrail for auditing.

•
CI/CD & Containers: Strong experience building secure automated pipelines via GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or AWS CodePipeline, alongside Docker and Kubernetes.

•
Data Orchestration & Processing: Strong proficiency with orchestration engines (Apache Airflow/MWAA, Step Functions) and modern data tools (dbt).

•
Coding & Databases: Advanced programming skills in Python and SQL, with a solid grasp of securing relational and NoSQL databases.

Soft Skills & Cultural Fit

•
Curious Explorer: Passionate about diving into the latest AWS whitepapers, learning new tooling, and experimenting with proof-of-concepts.

•
Security First Mindset: Naturally incorporates risk management and data privacy principles into every line of code and infrastructure design.

•
Challenged Driven: Thrives on debugging ambiguous system failures, performance tuning massive datasets, and solving untraditional cloud architecture problems.

Benefits
We offer

• Flexible working hours (self-managed)

• Annual bonus, subject to company performance

• Access to Udemy online training and opportunities to learn and grow within the role

At Mindera we use technology to build products we are proud of, with people we love.
Software Engineering Applications, including Web and Mobile, are at the core of what we do at Mindera .
We partner with our clients, to understand their products and deliver high-performance, resilient and scalable software systems that create an impact on their users and businesses across the world.
You get to work with a bunch of great people, and the whole team owns the project together.
Our culture reflects our lean and self-organisation attitude.
We encourage our colleagues to take risks, make decisions, work in a collaborative way and talk to everyone to enhance communication. We are proud of our work and we love to learn all and everything while navigatin

title: Hydrus - Voice Contributor - English (British)
description:
About the Project 
Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. We're looking for native-level speakers who can deliver natural, everyday-sounding speech - recordings that hold up whether you're reading a script or speaking spontaneously. 
Please note: the recordings you produce may be used to create synthesized, AI-generated voices for conversational AI products. Full details on how your data is collected, used, shared, and retained are set out in a Consent Form, which you'll review and sign before any paid session recording begins. 
 
What You'll Do If Selected: 
Two supervised sessions of approximately 4 hours each, guided in real time by a Session Director on a separate recording platform. 
Record scripted material in a natural, conversational tone - faithfully, without a polished, performed, or “announcer” delivery. 
Record unscripted, spontaneous speech on a given topic, matching the same warmth and pace as your scripted takes. 
Set up and manage your own recording space and equipment for session recording. 
Deliver all recordings entirely in the required language (with specific dialect), without code-switching into other languages or dialects. 
 
What We're Looking For 
Required 
Experience as a voice actor, actor, or theater performer, or a comparable performance background. 
Native or native-equivalent fluency in the required language (with specific dialect). 
Access to a quiet recording space, free of echo and background noise (acoustically treated for session recording, if selected). 
Owns or will acquire a dedicated, professional-grade microphone for the audition (e.g. RODE NT-USB Mini, Blue Yeti), upgrading to a qualifying USB condenser or XLR mic + audio interface for session recording if selected. Built-in laptop mics, AirPods, earbuds, and headsets are not accepted at any stage. 
Owns closed-back monitoring headphones (required for session recording if selected). 
Comfortable both self-directing for the audition and taking live direction from a Session Director in guided sessions. 
 
Preferred (nice to have, not required) 
Professional voice-over experience (dubbing/ADR, audiobook, podcasting) in a conversational rather than commercial/announcer register. 
Baseline audio hygiene: comfortable setting mic distance and catching noise, clipping, or distortion yourself. 
An existing home recording setup already treated for sound. 
 
Your Data & Privacy 
Before any session recording, you'll be asked to review and sign a Consent Form covering how your voice recordings are collected, used (including to train synthesized/AI voice models), shared with approved partners, retained, and how to exercise your data rights (access, correction, deletion, and more, depending on where you live). If you'd like to review these terms before applying, contact us and we'll share a copy in advance.

title: Senior Payment Accuracy Specialist (Healthcare)
description:
Overview
Cotiviti Healthcare is a leading provider of payment accuracy services to the most recognized companies in the healthcare and retail industries. We are seeking innovative thinkers and creative problem solvers who are interested in making a contribution to improving healthcare and want to be part of a team that is expanding rapidly and providing opportunities for career growth. If you want to make a difference and contribute to the improvement of healthcare payment integrity, consider an opportunity to join our healthcare recovery team as a Senior Payment Accuracy Specialist.
The Senior Specialist position is responsible for developing new and existing audit concepts, gaining client acceptance, training all audit levels to execute audit projects and evaluating the effectiveness of audit concepts. The goal of the position is to generate high quality recoverable claims for the benefit of Cotiviti and our clients. Conducts and documents more complex audit projects independently. This is the most senior skill level which may include supervisory responsibility. Assists Audit Managers in managing audit productivity, achieving expected quality and revenue goals. Considered a mentor, trainer, developer of less tenured Audit team members.
Responsibilities

• Generates and Develops New Audit Concepts. Utilizes healthcare and auditing experience to perform audit procedures that include identifying and defining issues, developing criteria, reviewing and analyzing evidence with the intent to audit standard medium and complex reports. Leader in concept development across multiple audit verticals. This includes specifying the concept, interact with client to test and gain acceptance. Will execute on the expansion of the concept based on customer requirements. Focused on growing concept approval.

• Develops New Tools and Processes. Collaborates with Business Optimization and audit team in developing new reports. Fosters and implements new ideas, approaches, and technological improvements to support and enhance audit production, communication and client satisfaction.

• Directs ownership for Quality Control. Reviews all level auditor claims prior to and after client submission. Set by the audit: for the auditing concept, audit against the expected level of quality and quantity (i.e.; hit rate, # claims written, ID per hour).

• Prepares Responses to Client Disputes. Provides oversight to audit team for verification of claims validation, insurance or employer validation in concise written or oral manner. Makes determinations based on advanced experience of client knowledge of contract terms, likelihood of acceptance recovery.

• Reviews provider Contracts. Subject matter expert in contracts and research requirements. Implements recommendations on contracts to fit projects within standard reports such as medical policies, state and federal statutes.

• Validates New Claim Types. With proficiency, utilizes audit tools to evaluate, document and validate to audit and client new claims and concept effectiveness. Ensures that any new and existing concepts are achieving desired goals in terms of recoveries, collectability and client acceptance.

• Auditor Development. Key participants in the development of audit staff. Actively trains audit team to execute basic, intermediate and complex audit projects with focus on new and existing audit concepts. May participate in auditor assessment, progression process, staffing functions.

• QA Claim Association/Concepts. Responsible for performing quality control process. Makes determinations based on advanced expertise and comprehension (knowledge) of claim categories, claim types. Ensures submission and execution of quality work, proper use of available proprietary software, reports and IT resources to conduct audits.

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed and is not to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, and skill

description:
About Yepoda

Clean K-Beauty Innovation. No compromises.

Yepoda is a clean K-Beauty brand that actually proves it works. We make Korean skincare without any of the compromises. Everything is clinically tested, 100% vegan, and formulated above EU standards. So you get the innovation and the results that K-Beauty is known for, plus a real commitment to sustainability. And we make it genuinely fun and easy to use - skincare you actually look forward to.

Founded in 2020 by Sander Joonyoung van Bladel and Veronika Strotmann, Yepoda is a certified B Corp™ and 1% for the Planet member, based in the heart of Berlin.Our products are available across Europe and the US, since March 2025, in Sephora Europe & since August 2026 in Sephora US - online and in over 1200 stores. With a team of 120+ brilliant individuals from around the world, we are actively shaping Yepoda's story every day.

Your Tasks:

- Manage daily procurement operations: Create, place and follow up on purchase orders, ensuring timely and accurate execution.

- Coordinate with suppliers: Maintain regular communication regarding order confirmations, lead times and delivery schedules.

- Ensure product availability: Monitor incoming deliveries, identify potential shortages and proactively address delays or supply disruptions.

- Maintain accurate data: Keep purchase orders, supplier information and delivery dates up to date in our ERP system (NetSuite).

- Support inventory management: Align purchasing activities with demand forecasts, inventory requirements and stock availability.

- Monitor procurement performance: Track relevant KPIs, including supplier delivery performance and product availability.

- Resolve operational issues: Investigate discrepancies, coordinate solutions with suppliers and internal stakeholders, and escalate risks when necessary.

- Contribute to continuous improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline procurement activities and improve process efficiency and data quality.

Your Profile:

- Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field.

- Ideally 2 years of relevant experience in procurement, purchasing or a related operational role.

- You work in a structured and reliable way, manage multiple priorities and consistently follow through on your tasks.

- You are comfortable working with numbers, identifying discrepancies and using data to support decisions.

- You understand the importance of accurate information, well-maintained systems and reliable processes.

- You take initiative, anticipate potential issues and communicate risks before they become problems.

- You communicate clearly and professionally with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

- You are confident using Excel or Google Sheets. Experience with ERP systems, ideally NetSuite, is an advantage.

- You are eager to learn, take ownership and continuously develop your procurement expertise.

- Fluent in English; Korean language skills are a plus.

What We Offer:

- Dynamic Environment: The opportunity to work in a start-up environment surrounded by a passionate and dedicated team.

- Accelerate Your Career: Take on responsibility from day 1, with room for professional growth and advancement as the company continues to expand.

- Inspiring Workspace: Located in the heart of Berlin's Prenzlauer Berg, a dog-friendly office, with free drinks and snacks.

- Hybrid Working: We understand that sometimes you get more stuff done from home and need a change of scenery.

- We Value Diversity: We seek to build an inclusive workplace that welcomes people from all different backgrounds. A welcoming, international, dedicated team with flat hierarchies and trust by default.

- Employee Discounts: You’ll get to enjoy the Yepoda products at a discount and share it with friends and family to keep your glow going!

title: AI & Innovation Lead, G&A
locationText: Remote in the United States · Remote
description:
At Sanity https://sanity.io/, we’re building the future of AI-powered Content Operations. Our AI Content Operating System gives teams the freedom to model, create, and automate content the way their business works, accelerating digital development and supercharging content operations efficiency. Companies like SKIMS, Figma, Riot Games, Anthropic, COMPLEX, Nordstrom, and Morning Brew use Sanity to power and automate their content operations.

In this role, you’ll join the Finance team as the AI & Innovation Lead, G&A, reporting to the CFO. You’ll sit in Finance with a dotted line to our Director of Systems Engineering. This role sits at the intersection of G&A operations, data, workflow automation, and AI. You bring the domain depth: you know how G&A teams actually work, where their processes and systems break, and which manual work eats their week. You’ll start with Finance, then quickly extend into People and the rest of G&A. You’ll prototype the fix yourself, vibe-coding agents, apps, and workflows on Sanity’s own platform and AI tools. Systems Engineering and the Data team back you on architecture, security, and production hardening, so your ideas become systems the business can rely on. If you’re a G&A operator who has already started rebuilding your own work with AI, and you want to do that for an entire G&A organization, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU WOULD DO:

- Shape and execute on the AI first transformation roadmap for G&A: map where G&A teams lose time, and decide what to build, buy, or automate first.

- Run intake, prioritization and stage-gates for the G&A transformation portfolio, with clear owners, decision rights and a regular exec review cadence

- Prototype agents, apps, and automations yourself on Sanity’s platform and AI tools, then partner with Systems Engineering to take the ones that work to production.

- Translate G&A processes into clear specs and prototypes for engineering: data flows, system of record, controls, edge cases, and what “done” looks like.

- Build for trust through controls, audit trails, access management, data quality, and human-in-the-loop review, so G&A teams and auditors can rely on what you ship.

- Partner with the Data and IT teams on the G&A systems and data infrastructure, connecting the systems G&A and our data warehouse together.

- Drive adoption across G&A: train teams, document the paved paths, and help each function run more of its own work with AI and retire legacy manual processes.

- Measure impact through hours saved, cycle times, error and exception rates, adoption, AI evals, and stakeholder feedback.

- Help shape the practices and culture of a young Systems Engineering team with a strong bias toward practical impact.

ABOUT YOU:

- Remote in North America (SF preferred).

- Deep G&A domain knowledge, ideally 8+ years in Finance, Accounting, People ops, or business operations at a software company.

- Hands-on experience applying AI to G&A work, for example leading an AI program for your function, automating a core process, or building agents for your own team.

- Comfortable building prototypes with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar). You don’t need to be a software engineer, and you’re not afraid of a terminal.

- Understands APIs, data flows, and how G&A systems connect: what moves between the ERP, HRIS, CRM, contract tools, and warehouse, and where it breaks.

- Excited by AI as an operating model, including agents, tool use, structured context, prompts, evals, and automation.

- Cares deeply about controls, accuracy, auditability, and systems G&A teams can confidently rely on.

- Program management strength: you can run a cross-functional roadmap, align stakeholders, and land change with teams that are busy running the business.

- Comfortable with ambiguity and able to turn loosely defined business problems into shipped solutions.

- Clear communicator who can explain G&A processes to engineers and technical tradeoffs to G&A teams.

NICE TO

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🐙 WHERE YOU'LL FIT IN

We're looking for a subject matter expert in payments to lead payments delivery for our clients in Japan. You'll know how money moves in Japan, from traditional channels to newer ones, and you'll turn that into tangible outcomes for our clients.

You'll be a hands-on individual contributor in a flat, agile team, working with Kraken's engineers and the client's teams. Our clients are large, established Japanese utilities with legacy systems and sometimes limited payments expertise. You’ll be looked at by our teams, and the clients, as an expert and a leader.

Payments are only part of the picture. You'll also be in conversations about debt management and the wider process of collecting money from customers, both those in arrears and those who pay on time.

- Leading payments implementations from discovery to go-live and beyond

- Understanding clients’ legacy systems and desired payments outcomes, and turning them into practical requirements and realistic plans

- Balancing operational, commercial and technical pressures to deliver the right solution for the client and for Kraken

- Recommending the right payment channels, integrations and reconciliation approach

- Advising on collections and debt management alongside payments

- Coaching colleagues on payments

Essential

- Led payments implementations end to end, as the driver rather not just a team member

- Expert knowledge of payments in Japan, from traditional channels (e.g. VAN, bank transfer) to newer providers (e.g. Stripe, Adyen, GMO)

- Background in a technology or software environment

- Ability to turn legacy systems and business problems into clear requirements

- Comfortable discussing debt management and collections with clients

- Experience explaining payments clearly to non-technical clients

- Credible in front of senior stakeholders

- Fluent Japanese and business level of English

- Willing to travel

Helpful
